brewing.notes: A safe starting point for ripe pu-erh: rinse once or twice, boiling water.

description:
A ripe pu-erh from Yunnan whose name means caravan leader.

This is a way of preparing tea more than a tea you buy under one name, so the recipe and the base tea change from one maker to the next.
history: A 2012 production is known. Little more is documented about it.
processing: Made from a ripe pu-erh base tea according to the recipe; the method varies.
harvest_season: Not tied to a harvest: it depends on the base tea.
appearance_dry: Usually dark brown leaf, loose or pressed.
taste_profile: Expect what ripe pu-erh usually gives: smooth, earthy and sweet.
